Information since September points to a strong labor market and moderate growth, but capex and exports are weak and inflation remains below 2 percent. Cutting the federal funds rate to 1.5–1.75 percent and lowering IORB to 1.55 percent, alongside Treasury bill purchases to maintain ample reserves and smooth money markets, are consistent with interest-rate transmission in modern NK frameworks (e.g., Woodford 2003) and with evidence that investment is sensitive to financing conditions and internal liquidity (Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein 1994). With market-based inflation compensation low, the forward-looking Phillips curve (Galí and Gertler 1999) underscores the role of expected inflation, supporting a dovish stance to re-anchor inflation near the symmetric 2 percent objective. Overall, the tone is cautiously supportive: policy easing offsets demand headwinds, but subdued investment and soft inflation expectations temper the outlook.
